correctness.rationale: At the frozen tree 96a9fe26, reconstructed the orientation-bit convention and the unique source strongly connected component recurrence: each source component U contributes its signed internal strong-tournament sum and the forced outward cross-arc sign. An independent 2^15-orientation reachability enumeration followed by exact 15-bit integer Walsh transform reproduced 22,320 strong tournaments, the complete 12-level absolute coefficient distribution, 24,352 zero coefficients and 8,416 nonzeros. Independently enumerated all S_6 edge-support permutation orbits and orientation-reversal parity; obtained 156 orbits, two exceptional eight-edge zero orbits represented by 958 and 1883, 360 members each, and exactly 720 symmetry-unforced zeros. The inverse transform of nonzero-frequency support has absolute numerator sum 1,399,040 and hence projection norm 1,399,040/32768=5465/128. Translation averaging of arbitrary projections onto the invariant Fourier range proves unrestricted optimality. Actual code and certificates checked at the assigned Git tree: verify_tournament_enumeration.cpp, verify_tournament_scc.cpp, walsh_coefficients.txt (32,768 coefficients), tournament_support_orbits.tsv (156 rows). The statement classifies only the two specifically defined symmetry-forcing mechanisms, not all conceivable identities.

value.rationale: Strong connectivity is a basic tournament invariant, and the first moderate complete orientation cube where nontrivial symmetry-unforced cancellation can be classified is mathematically natural. Separating exactly 720 zeros in two eight-edge support orbits from 23,632 symmetry-forced zeros produces a structural, precisely reproducible boundary, while rank and sharp endpoint projection norm quantify Fourier recovery. The calculation is finite but not an arbitrary slice or merely reprinting the 22,320 tournament count.
